brief: GS Industrials & Materials morning note ahead of the September 16 FOMC decision. The 25bp hike is priced at 93% and treated as a non-event; the live question is whether the Fed validates a hiking cycle now priced at roughly 3.5 hikes through next summer, with GIR expecting a 10-8 dot-plot majority for one hike in 2026 because some voters are ambivalent about hiking or wary of pushing expectations higher. The author reads Chair Warsh's reaction function as the key signal and argues enough hikes are already priced unless oil reaches $150. Prime data shows Industrials among the most net-sold sectors this month and YTD, driven by short sales outpacing long buys, with Electrical Equipment/Machinery hit hardest and net allocation to US Power stocks at two-year lows. On earnings, JBHT signaled EPS down 5-10% sequentially on cost headwinds, echoing LECO's lowered margin guidance and CARR's reiterated earnings despite a firmer topline. Separately, GIR cut Tesla's 3Q26 delivery forecast to 435K from 490K on weaker China/US/Europe trends, though export markets and a 4Q Model Y L ramp could lift deliveries qoq. FTAI and DHI announced buybacks; SPXC announced an acquisition.
